families.label: You stopped at an earlier step instead of finishing the problem.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice is a value the student would get partway through a correct solution, such as a total instead of the remaining amount, or the amount left instead of the amount lost.

families.label: You found a real value from the problem, but not the one the question asked for.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice is a different quantity from the same setup, such as the other angle, the area instead of the height, the x-intercept instead of k, the wrong variable or trig ratio, a percentage instead of a count, or a sum of categories instead of one category.

families.label: You used a number or relationship that isn't the one the problem gave.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice comes from swapping a given value or equation for a different one, such as 270 instead of 370, a diameter of 2√22 instead of 22, a different equation, or the wrong discount rates.

families.label: You made a mistake while rewriting or calculating an expression.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice comes from a procedural slip such as distributing incorrectly, an invalid rearrangement, mixing up terms and factors, dropping a coefficient, or a basic arithmetic or percent calculation error.

families.label: You mixed up what a feature of the equation or graph means, such as slope, intercept, direction, or shape.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice has the wrong slope, y-intercept, sign of slope, curvature, or points compared with the relationship described, including tables or equations that match a different line.

families.label: Your answer meets some of the conditions but not all of them. Check it against every requirement.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice satisfies only part of what the problem requires, such as ≤50 but not even, or when substituting the choice back in shows it fails a condition like an inequality, the parallel-lines condition, a given perimeter, or no solution versus infinitely many solutions.

families.label: You answered the opposite case: "not" instead of "is," "less" instead of "greater," or the reverse.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice answers the complement or reverse of the condition asked, such as either versus neither, other responses versus the named responses, the wrong side of an inequality, or the opposite age group.

families.label: You drew a conclusion that goes further than the evidence supports.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice claims more than the text or data justify, such as an inference the passage never supports, details a quotation doesn't contain, a claim an author wouldn't accept, generalizing a sample beyond the population sampled, or treating an estimate with a margin of error as exact.

families.label: Your answer conflicts with what the text actually says. Reread the key detail.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice contradicts, reverses, or misattributes information stated in the passage, including word choices whose meaning clashes with the surrounding context or the contrast the text sets up.

families.label: You picked something the text mentions, but it isn't the main point or the stated goal.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice focuses on an incidental detail rather than the central idea, or doesn't accomplish the task the question names, such as comparing, reiterating, or describing a shared feature.

families.label: You chose a transition that signals the wrong relationship between the ideas.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice is a transition that signals contrast, addition, example, or sequence, but the two sentences actually have a different logical relationship.

families.label: You joined or split clauses with the wrong punctuation.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice creates a run-on or comma splice, fuses independent clauses without the required punctuation, or places punctuation at a grammatically incoherent point.

families.label: Your verb doesn't agree with its subject or isn't in the right form.
families.when: Assign when the wrong choice has a subject-verb number mismatch or uses a nonfinite form, such as an infinitive, where a conjugated main verb is required.

families.label: This mistake doesn't match a common pattern. Review the explanation for this question.
families.when: Assign when the rationale only says the choice is wrong or describes it without naming a recognizable error pattern.
